tasks.short: Notice signs of abuse or neglect and talk with the client, consult a colleague on the steps, write the report of facts observed, check it, and report to the authorities.

steps.what: Community health worker notices signs of abuse or neglect and talks with the client
Community health worker consults a colleague on the reporting steps
Community health worker writes the report of incidences and facts observed
Community health worker checks the final report: facts observed, what is shared and the authority it goes to
Community health worker reports abuse or neglect to authorities

tasks.design: The client record ({OTHER}) has a report form that follows the reporting code's steps and fills in the client's details and earlier contacts, so the worker writes only the facts observed. No software drafts the facts. Noticing signs, consulting a colleague, checking the report and reporting to the authority stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were written from scratch, with client details copied in by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Client record systems hold report forms that fill known details.
tasks.still_hard: Facts must be described carefully and without judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding to report while keeping the client's trust.

evidence.claim: Client record systems can hold report forms that fill known client details.
Dutch professionals must follow a reporting code for domestic violence and child abuse.
Health data are special category data; sharing needs a legal basis.

assumptions: Boundary: from the home visit to the authority informed; the authority's investigation is outside.
Input contract: client record current; fallback is writing from scratch.
Every report decision stays with the worker. s3 keeps 75 because the worker writes the facts observed; the form fills client details and earlier contacts.
research_questions: Do authorities ask fewer follow-up questions?

incremental.description: Community health worker keeps the report form in step with the code.

approvals.approved_version: The report of facts observed exactly as checked by the worker in s4, made once to the authority named in the reporting code; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex cases with incomplete records, where the form fills little, so s3 keeps 90 (2.0); high: clients with full records (5.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit clients and observe eating, weigh and measure them, compare values with growth or weight charts, and advise on nutrition.

steps.what: Community health worker visits clients and monitors nutrition of high-risk groups
Community health worker weighs and measures clients and notes the values: on paper and typed into the record later today, on the tablet after the change
Community health worker compares values with growth or weight charts by hand
Community health worker advises clients on nutrition

tasks.design: Weight and height go straight into the client record on a tablet ({OTHER}), which plots them on the right growth or weight chart and flags loss beyond a set limit, so values are not written on paper and charted by hand. Visiting, observing and advising stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Values were written on paper and compared with charts by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Client record apps plot growth and weight charts with fixed limits.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing an empty fridge that the numbers do not show.

evidence.claim: Client record apps can plot growth and weight charts and flag changes beyond set limits.
Health data are special category data; processing needs a legal basis.

assumptions: Boundary: from the visit due to advice given; treatment is outside.
Input contract: tablets for field workers; fallback is paper.

Visiting, measuring and advising do not change. s2 keeps 75 because weighing, measuring and noting each value stay; only typing paper values into the record later goes. s3 keeps 10 for reading the plotted chart and the flags.

incremental.description: Community health worker enters values later where there is no signal.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: tablets are often not at hand or without signal, so paper stays for many visits and s2 keeps 90 and s3 keeps 60 (5.0); high: tablets used at most visits (12.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write visit notes, update the client's plan, fill referral and application forms, and file paper forms and letters in the client folder.

steps.what: Community health worker asks the client's consent to record the visit and starts the recording
Community health worker writes notes after each visit

loop.input: The recorded visit, when the client consents.
loop.output: A draft visit note in the record's structure.
loop.check: A validator flags any risk statement (suicide, violence, abuse) not in the transcript. The worker reads every note against the transcript and the visit, checks that it says what happened and nothing more, and edits and approves it before saving.
loop.stop: One draft per visit; if the client declines recording or the draft is rejected, the worker writes the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: Visits are told in the client's words; a form does not capture them.

steps.what: Community health worker updates the client's plans
Community health worker fills appropriate forms by copying client details
Community health worker scans and files paper letters that still arrive; completed forms are stored in the record

tasks.design: With the client's consent, a scribe in the client record ({OTHER}) drafts the visit note from the recorded visit; a validator flags any risk statement not in the transcript, and the worker edits and approves every note. Referral and application forms fill client details from the record, and completed forms are stored in the record, so paper is not filed. Updating the plan stays with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after visits, forms filled by hand and paper filed.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes draft notes from recorded visits; records prefill forms.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can invent statements, including risk statements.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a plan the client agrees with.
tasks.altitude: The worker checks drafts instead of typing notes.

evidence.claim: Rapportage-assistent records the intake and drafts the report with language models; a worker checks every output.
Somerset Council's Magic Notes pilot with 20 staff reported about 11 hours a week saved per practitioner and weekly admin time down 46%; self-reported.
UK social workers found invented suicidal ideation in AI-drafted notes.
Recording staff conversations needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the visit done to the folder updated; decisions on care are outside.
Input contract: client consent for recording; fallback is typing notes.
The worker approves every note. About 70% of clients consent to recording; s1 is priced at that share. s4 keeps 20 for paper letters from others.
A DPIA and works council consent come before recording.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag a risk statement?

already_counted.description: Community health worker edits drafted notes.

incremental.description: No new work: asking consent is shown as step s0.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of clients decline recording and much post still arrives on paper, so s1 keeps 75 and s4 keeps 50 (33.5); high: 70% consent as assumed (46.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find clients with open actions from paper lists, phone them to check progress, visit those who cannot be reached, and record the outcome.

steps.what: Community health worker finds clients with open actions from paper lists
Community health worker contacts clients by phone to ensure they completed required actions
Community health worker visits clients in person who cannot be reached
Community health worker records the follow-up outcome

tasks.design: Actions agreed with clients are stored in the client record ({OTHER}) with a due date, and a daily follow-up list shows who is due, so the worker does not search paper lists. The worker records the outcome as today; it is a first record and keeps its time. Phoning and visiting clients stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Open actions were tracked on paper and outcomes written in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Client records hold actions with due dates and follow-up lists.
tasks.still_hard: Actions agreed informally do not get a due date.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing why a client did not go to the appointment.

evidence.claim: Client record systems can hold actions with due dates and produce follow-up lists.
Health data are special category data; processing needs a legal basis.

assumptions: Boundary: from the follow-up due to the outcome recorded; new plans are outside.
Input contract: actions entered with due dates; fallback is paper lists.
Phoning, visiting and recording the outcome do not change.
research_questions: Are follow-ups done on time more often?

incremental.description: Community health worker enters due dates for agreed actions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: due dates are often not entered, so paper lists stay in use and s1 keeps 60 (5.0); high: due dates entered as designed (11.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The community health worker keeps visiting, advising, reporting concerns and following up clients; typed notes, paper charts, copied forms and paper lists shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted notes for invented statements
role.ambitious_version: A worker with more time with clients.
